answer: Delayed shared-seed admission.** Each epoch, agents commit to join; the protocol later reveals a randomness beacon derived from a posted sonnet-size entropy block, and only agents whose commitment survives a hash-ordered drawing are admitted. Since seeds stay hidden until after commitments lock, an attacker cannot precompute which clones land in the oasis of admitted slots. Each clone costs a fresh commitment and a full epoch wait, and rejected copies must be re-entered blind, so every identity pays real time plus a paid fee per attempt, like fording a river that reshuffles each crossing.
